notes: No published anechoic curve exists for the 15-inch M2 MacBook Air mic array; this is an estimate from the known behaviour of Apple's MEMS capsule arrays (M1/M2 MacBooks) captured raw with no macOS DSP. Reasonably known: flat within about +/-1-2 dB from 100 Hz to 4 kHz. Guessed: low-frequency vent roll-off (-3 dB point anywhere 50-120 Hz, modelled here around 80 Hz) and the port/Helmholtz treble bump (+4 to +8 dB, centre 8-14 kHz, modelled as +5.5 dB at 10 kHz) followed by fall-off toward 20 kHz. Averaging the three capsules reduces capsule variation but not the shared port resonance. Placement on a desk/lid geometry adds +/-2-3 dB ripple above ~2 kHz not included here. Trust polarity and room-mode verdicts in the 100 Hz-4 kHz band; treat <60 Hz and >10 kHz as indicative only. A one-off comparison against a calibrated mic (e.g. UMIK-1) in the measuring position would upgrade this to medium/high confidence.
